content.text: the medial canthus of the eye,
: contrast imaging of lacrimal sac & nasolacrimal duct
swelling/erythema over lacrimal gland (lat upper eyelid)
: viral = USU self-limiting, broad-spectrum ABX for bact
▪︎infection involving the fat + ocular muscles in the orbit but ⍉the globe
▪︎distinguished from preseptal cellulitis by ophthalmoplegia, pain w/ eye movements, + proptosis
▪︎MC 2° to bacterial rhinosinusitis (esp ethmoid) spreading to the medial orbit; there is almost always rhinosinusitis
▪︎also: orbital trauma w/ fracture/foreign body · orbital surgery · odontogenic infection · dacryocystitis · middle ear/face infection · infected mucocele
S/SXS: pain, lid erythema, restricted + painful eye movements, ⇣visual acuity, afferent pupillary defect, fever, proptosis, + conjunctival chemosis
Complications: orbital abscess, vision loss, intracranial infection (meningitis, septic cavernous sinus thrombosis)
DX: clin + confirmed w/ CT scan
▪︎ask about recent URI, recent ophthalmic surgery, chronic sinusitis, thick nasal secretions, + dental dz
▪︎immediate CT scan of the head incl the sinuses → look for complications (subperiosteal abscess, intracranial extension)
▪︎CT findings indicating orbital cellulitis: inflammation of the extraocular muscles, fat stranding, + anterior displacement of the globe
▪︎blood cultures should be obtained but are typically negative
▪︎CBC, when abnormal: leukocytes w/ a predominance of neutrophils
TX: broad-spectrum IV abx incl MRSA coverage; initial tx should be aggressive to prevent massive proptosis, meningitis, blindness, or septic cavernous sinus thrombosis
▪︎IV vancomycin + ceftriaxone or cefotaxime = recommended initial tx in a pt w/o intracranial involvement
▪︎vancomycin is given in conjunction w/ ceftriaxone or cefotaxime, ⍉as a single agent
▪︎intracranial involvement or evidence of rhinosinusitis → metronidazole may be added for anaerobic coverage
▪︎improvement should be seen w/in 24–48 hrs; once afebrile + eyelid/orbit findings substantially improved → transition to oral therapy as indicated (ex, TMP-SMX)
▪︎poor response to tx → surgical biopsy may be indicated; surgical drainage also indicated for abscesses >10 mm, those that fail to respond to abx, or those that threaten vision
▪︎majority of pts respond rapidly to appropriate tx
▪︎infection of the anterior portion of the eyelid
▪︎vs orbital cellulitis: no pain w/ eye movements, no proptosis, no ophthalmoplegia, no vision impairment
S/SXS: eyelid swelling (± erythema); eye pain/tenderness may be present
